scope: Representation of source-defined generic chemical classes; not a new chemical identity, exact structure or specific methyltransferase claim.
baseline_behavior: At base0919419 the closed category enum has no general chemical_entity option. Existing uncategorized MetaCyc participants correctly fall back to biolink:NamedThing and neutral graph styling; they are not exported as reactions. The change preserves the source-supported general chemical kind without asserting small-molecule, polymer or cofactor specificity.

sources.inspected_assertion: The source describes methylation targets spanning nucleic acids, proteins, phospholipids, biological amines and small molecules.
The native reaction transfers a methyl group from SAM to an unspecified acceptor; specific acceptor reactions are special cases.
The native compound class leaves the identity of the methyl donor or acceptor unknown or undefined.
The native class represents methylated forms without selecting one biological substrate.

implementation.kgx: biolink:ChemicalEntity; source_category and per-record source_contexts retain chemical_entity
implementation.diagram: Existing chemical styling; exact generic label and component navigation retained
implementation.identifier_policy: Unchanged; every named native class must independently resolve to its issuing authority.

focused_validation.new_regression: Generic native input/output classes survive both validators, exact KGX categories and contexts, chemical SVG styling and component navigation; concrete water remains SmallMolecule. Generic chemical subjects do not bypass enzyme-only cofactor constraints.
focused_validation.lint: Three initial style findings corrected; subsequent ruff check of changed Python files passed. Full frozen-corpus gates remain separate.

limits: This rationale is integration-agent analysis, not the independent scientific review.
No supported subtype is broadened and no existing pathway record is changed by this category addition.
